episode_title: The $1+ Billion Dollar Marketing Expert: "My $100M Portfolio's #1 Secret To 5X-10X Your Business"

real_qa.q: What is Bad Marketing's total managed client revenue?
real_qa.r: Bad Marketing collectively manages $2 billion in revenue across client businesses. The agency works behind the scenes for major brands and grows revenue for companies as large as $400-500 million annually, with one client famously receiving emails from Yeezy that the team likely sent.

real_qa.q: How did Eddie Malouf close $80,000 in flooring sales at age 14-15 on a single Saturday?
real_qa.r: Eddie spent six hours studying product information on every flooring and tile sample in the showroom before selling, then focused on identifying each customer's specific problem rather than overselling features. He realized customers were impressed by his depth of knowledge despite his young age, and he would recommend only the products that solved their particular needs, closing deals while competitors averaged $10,000 that day.
real_qa.requete: Eddie Malouf $80000 flooring sales story age

real_qa.q: What is the core difference between a $1 million business and a $10 million business according to Eddie Malouf?
real_qa.r: The difference is not more products but a different way to sell the same product. For example, a supplement company can generate $3 million by positioning the product for gut health and another $5 million by targeting a different segment for weight loss—same product, different frame, more revenue. There are companies built on a single billion-dollar angle simply by reframing the same offering.

real_qa.q: How did Eddie Malouf secure distribution contracts with major supplement companies at age 20 with zero experience?
real_qa.r: He first signed 100 massive fitness influencers (500k-700k followers each) in the Middle East to exclusive commission-based promotion contracts, then approached 20 supplement companies at the Mr. Olympia convention in Las Vegas with a 40-page document proving he had guaranteed distribution and influencer reach. Out of these meetings, 15 companies including EHP Labs and Optimum Nutrition signed exclusivity contracts making him sole distributor for all Middle Eastern countries.
real_qa.requete: Eddie Malouf supplement distribution contract Mr. Olympia

real_qa.q: Why did Eddie Malouf's supplement distribution business in the Middle East ultimately fail to launch?
real_qa.r: Despite securing regulatory paperwork and spending three months assembling an impossible list of requirements, he flew to Lebanon with 140 pounds of samples and documentation to submit to the Ministry of Health but was blocked by competitors who bribed government officials to prevent his entry. After being ignored for six hours and seeing his competitor's name on the desk with money, he abandoned the venture after spending a week in Lebanon, marking his lowest point before pivoting to what became Bad Marketing.
real_qa.requete: Eddie Malouf Lebanon supplement Ministry Health blocked

guest.bio_context: Eddie Malouf grew up in a family of Lebanese immigrants who started a flooring company; his parents never held traditional jobs, instilling an entrepreneurial mindset from childhood. At age 14-15, he sold $80,000 worth of flooring in a single Saturday while his peers averaged $10,000, using deep product knowledge to identify customer problems. He went on to build multiple eight-figure businesses and now manages over $1 billion in collective client revenue through Bad Marketing, an e-commerce advertising agency that works with brands as large as $400-500 million annually.

real_quote: The difference between a $1 million business and a $10 million business is not more products. It's a different way to sell the same product you currently have.
